title: Ontario Conservative MP Larry Brock resigns from Parliament | CBC News
text: Conservative MP Larry Brock to resign from Parliament in September Conservative MP Larry Brock says he'll be resigning from the House of Commons next month. Brock, the MP for the Ontario riding of Brantford—Brant South—Six Nations, was elected to Parliament in two consecutive elections — first in 2021, and again in 2025. He served as an assistant Crown attorney prior to being elected to the House of Commons. In a letter posted to social media on Thursday, Brock said he'd "accepted an opportunity to return directly to the frontlines of justice at the Brantford Crown Attorney's office." pic.twitter.com/pcW5HZnwnO His resignation will take effect on Sept. 18, according to the letter announcing his exit. Conservative Leader Pierre Poilievre posted a brief message on X, thanking Brock for his work as an MP. "My ardent wish is for you and your family to have all the success and happiness in the world. God bless, my friend," Poilievre said in his post. Conservative MPs publicly back Poilievre as leader even after recent stumbles 'Throw them out' of Parliament: Poilievre in favour of recall petition for floor-crossers The Conservatives won the second-most seats in the 2025 federal election, but the party has seen seven MPs — Brock included — leave its federal caucus since that time. Four MPs from the Conservative benches crossed the floor to join the governing Liberals — Chris d'Entremont, Michael Ma, Matt Jeneroux and Marilyn Gladu. Richard Martel, the now-former MP for the Quebec riding of Chicoutimi—Le Fjord, was appointed to the Senate by Prime Minister Mark Carney in July. Cathay Wagantall, a Conservative MP since 2015, is resigning her seat of Yorkton—Melville in Saskatchewan effective Aug. 31. Audience Relations, CBC P.O.
